text:
To decide whether a compound is optically active we ask whether the individual molecule is chiral (i.e. not related to its mirror image by any symmetry operation such as an internal mirror plane, a centre of inversion, or an Sn axis).  

1. (Z)-1-chloro-2-methylbut-1-ene  
   ClCH=C(CH₃)-CH₂-CH₃ has no stereogenic centre, and the C=C plane is a plane of symmetry.  
   → achiral.

2. (3aR,7aS,E)-8-(chloromethylene)hexahydro-4,7-methano-isobenzofuran-1,3-dione  
   Two specified stereogenic bridgehead centres (3aR,7aS) and no internal symmetry survive the extra exocyclic substituent.  
   → chiral → optically active.

3. (2R,3S)-2,3-dimethylsuccinic acid  
   HOOC-CH*(CH₃)-CH*(CH₃)-COOH with 2R,3S is a meso form; a mirror plane passes through the middle of the molecule.  
   → achiral.

4. (2R,3R)-2,3-dimethylsuccinic acid  
   The RR (and likewise SS) form lacks that mirror plane → chiral → optically active.

5. (R)-cyclohex-3-en-1-ol  
   Carbon-1 is a single stereogenic centre; the 3,4-double bond destroys any possible internal mirror plane (C₂ and C₆ are not equivalent).  
   → chiral → optically active.

6. (1S,3S,5S)-cyclohexane-1,3,5-triol  
   With OH groups arranged cis (all on the same side) the chair conformer is a “propeller’’; it possesses a C₃ axis but no mirror plane or Sn axis, so the S,S,S and R,R,R forms are enantiomers. Chair flipping does not interchange them.  
   → chiral → optically active.

7. 1-cyclopentyl-3-methylbutan-1-one  
   Carbon-3 (-CH(CH₃)-) is bound to three different carbon groups (CH₃, CH₂-C=O-cyclopentyl, and the rest of the chain) and to H → stereogenic; no symmetry element relates the two sides of the chain.  
   → chiral → optically active.

Summary  
Optically active: compounds 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 = 5 compounds.

Answer: A
